decisions.statement: A page's uncommitted values sit in the file whose only section is `uncommitted`.
A page's uncommitted values are written and read as a page's own values are.
These values are written here rather than by a landing.
The gate refuses a file no page claims.
Which page this file belongs to is read from this file's name.
The page beside this file claims this file where this file is there.
A file written here reaches the listing at the next settle over its page.
A file taken away here leaves the listing at that same settle.
The file is replaced by writing a scratch file beside that file and renaming that scratch file over.
A replacement keeps the mode the replaced file already had.
A file written where no file was there takes the mode the umask gives.
A page no file sits beside carries no uncommitted values rather than failing to read the values.
A file that will not load or loads declaring nothing is refused rather than read as empty.
The exported name has the page's own name.
Every write takes a lock keyed on the file that write writes.
The lock is a `.lock` directory beside the file.
The lock is taken by one create that fails where the lock is already there.
The lock is released however the act inside the lock ends.
Git ignores every `.lock`.
The lock names the process that took the lock and the moment that process started.
A lock whose holder is gone is taken rather than waited on.
A lock naming no holder that can be read is taken once that lock has been there too long.
A write takes away every scratch file beside the file before writing its own scratch file.
A scratch file there while the lock is held is dead, whatever process left that scratch file.
A write that dies before its rename leaves a scratch file the next write takes away.
Values merge key by key into the values already there.
Dropping names the keys to take away.
Taking the whole file away is its own act under its own name.
Taking the whole file away takes away every scratch file beside that file too.
A page's whole value merges the uncommitted values into the values the commit has.
A key held both ways is answered as the uncommitted value.
A file already read is read again once its moment or its size has changed.
A reader takes no lock.
Nothing asks whether the process that left a scratch file is alive.
A change is handed the values already there and answers the values to write, inside the lock.

definition: the values a page carries that the commit does not hold
